messages.content:
You plan the work for one part of a course assignment or project. A team of AI agents will carry
it out: a coding agent builds, a testing agent tests. Design, documentation and the final review are planned
separately, so do not add those steps.

Return JSON with "steps", "research_questions", "not_plannable" and "open_questions".

Each step:
- key: a short local name ("b1", "b2" for build steps, "t1", "t2" for test steps).
- title: an imperative title of at most 8 words ("Broadcast messages to all clients").
- description: one or two sentences on what to do.
- phase: "implement" (build something) or "test" (check that it works).
- requirement_ids: the ids of the requirements the step delivers or checks. Use only ids from the list.
- acceptance_criteria: 1-4 concrete, checkable statements taken from the requirements, keeping their numbers
  ("at least 10 clients connected at the same time").
- effort_hours: a rough estimate for one student (0.5 to 16).
- depends_on: keys of steps in your answer whose result this step needs (a test needs what it tests; the client
  may need the server's protocol). Never depend on a later step in a circle.
- group: a 1-3 word feature name shared by related steps ("Messaging").

Rules:
- Every requirement id in the list must appear in at least one step, unless it is in not_plannable.
- Use as few steps as the work needs: a build step covers 1-4 closely related requirements that one person would
  build together; a test step checks one feature group (it may check several build steps).
- Quality requirements (speed, robustness, usability) usually belong to test steps.
- Writing tests, scripts or documents that a requirement asks for is a build step.
- Dependencies: a step that uses, extends, tests or describes what another step makes depends on it (the command-line
  interface needs the logic it calls; unit tests need the code they test; code implementing a model needs the model).
- At most 12 steps. Never invent requirements, numbers, tools or extra features.
- research_questions: 2-5 specific questions the team must answer before designing (techniques, libraries the
  constraints allow, known pitfalls).
- not_plannable: requirements an AI agent cannot carry out (a live demo, handing in on a portal), with a reason.
- open_questions: anything unclear or contradictory (an empty list if nothing is).

Project kind: software.
The whole request is one part.

Requirements:
R1 [must, functional] Identify the actors that interact with the garage system. (section: Part A: Requirements analysis)
R2 [must, functional] For each actor, describe at least two goals in one sentence each. (section: Part A: Requirements analysis)
R3 [must, functional] The domain model must cover levels and parking spots of different sizes. (section: Part B: Domain model)
R4 [must, functional] The domain model must cover vehicles and their size classes. (section: Part B: Domain model)
R5 [must, functional] The domain model must cover tickets with entry and exit times. (section: Part B: Domain model)
R6 [must, functional] The domain model must cover payments for a ticket. (section: Part B: Domain model)
R7 [must, functional] Implement the domain model in an object‑oriented language of your choice. (section: Part C: Implementation)
R8 [must, functional] Assign the smallest free spot that fits a vehicle. (section: Part C: Implementation)
R9 [must, functional] Issue a ticket when a vehicle enters. (section: Part C: Implementation)
R10 [must, functional] Calculate the fee from the entry and exit times. (section: Part C: Implementation)
R11 [must, functional] Free the spot when the vehicle leaves. (section: Part C: Implementation)
R12 [should, non-functional] The fee rules should be easy to change without editing the ticket class. (section: Part C: Implementation)
R13 [should, functional] The command‑line interface must support parking a vehicle. (section: Part D: Command-line interface)
R14 [should, functional] The command‑line interface must support removing a vehicle and printing its fee. (section: Part D: Command-line interface)
R15 [should, functional] The command‑line interface must support showing the free spots on each level. (section: Part D: Command-line interface)

Constraints (respect them, do not make steps for them):
C1 [process] Discuss your ideas with your lab partner, sketch them on paper first, and only then move on to the computer.
C2 [technology] Use only the standard library of your language.

response.text:
{
  "steps": [
    {
      "key": "b1",
      "title": "Design domain model classes",
      "description": "Create class diagrams for levels, parking spots, vehicles, tickets and payments covering required attributes and relationships.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Domain model includes levels and parking spots of different sizes (R3)",
        "Domain model includes vehicles and their size classes (R4)",
        "Domain model includes tickets with entry and exit times (R5)",
        "Domain model includes payments for a ticket (R6)"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 3,
      "depends_on": [],
      "group": "Model Design"
    },
    {
      "key": "b2",
      "title": "Implement domain model and core logic",
      "description": "Code the classes, spot assignment, ticket issuance, fee calculation and spot release using only the standard library.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R7", "R8", "R9", "R10", "R11", "R12"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Domain model is implemented in an OO language (R7)",
        "System assigns the smallest free spot that fits a vehicle (R8)",
        "System issues a ticket when a vehicle enters (R9)",
        "System calculates the fee from entry and exit times (R10)",
        "System frees the spot when the vehicle leaves (R11)",
        "Fee rules can be changed without editing the ticket class (R12)"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 6,
      "depends_on": ["b1"],
      "group": "Implementation"
    },
    {
      "key": "b3",
      "title": "Implement command‑line interface",
      "description": "Add CLI commands to park a vehicle, remove a vehicle (printing its fee) and display free spots per level.",
      "phase": "implement",
      "requirement_ids": ["R13", "R14", "R15"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "CLI supports parking a vehicle (R13)",
        "CLI supports removing a vehicle and printing its fee (R14)",
        "CLI supports showing the free spots on each level (R15)"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 4,
      "depends_on": ["b2"],
      "group": "CLI"
    },
    {
      "key": "t1",
      "title": "Write unit tests for core logic",
      "description": "Create automated tests that verify spot assignment, ticket issuance, fee calculation and spot release work as specified.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R8", "R9", "R10", "R11", "R12"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Test confirms the smallest suitable spot is assigned (R8)",
        "Test confirms a ticket is created on vehicle entry (R9)",
        "Test confirms fee is correctly calculated from times (R10)",
        "Test confirms the spot becomes free after vehicle leaves (R11)",
        "Test confirms fee rules can be altered without modifying ticket code (R12)"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 3,
      "depends_on": ["b2"],
      "group": "Testing"
    },
    {
      "key": "t2",
      "title": "Write integration tests for CLI",
      "description": "Automate end‑to‑end scenarios that exercise the CLI commands and validate their output.",
      "phase": "test",
      "requirement_ids": ["R13", "R14", "R15"],
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "CLI test parks a vehicle and reports success (R13)",
        "CLI test removes a vehicle and prints the correct fee (R14)",
        "CLI test lists free spots per level accurately (R15)"
      ],
      "effort_hours": 2,
      "depends_on": ["b3"],
      "group": "Testing"
    }
  ],
  "research_questions": [
    "Which standard‑library data structures best model hierarchical levels and spot collections?",
    "How to implement fee‑rule configurability (e.g., strategy pattern) without external libraries?",
    "What is the most reliable way to parse command‑line arguments using only the standard library?"
  ],
  "not_plannable": [],
  "open_questions": []
}
